requirement:
The test and run details required by
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary` MUST remain available on
demand in the combined coverage overview rather than expanded by default.
rationale:
**Obligation.** `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.combined.details` has two parts. The test and run details that `requirements.test-coverage.index.summary` requires (binary, test, attempt, capture time, command, selection, outcome, revisions, dirty state) MUST stay available in the combined overview. They MUST be on demand, not expanded by default.

**Test.** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[file_maps_union_process_locations_and_filter_unexecuted_test_files]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It builds a fixture run and renders the combined index through `populate`. It then renders the index Markdown to HTML with pulldown_cmark and checks:
- **Available on demand.** The HTML contains `<details class="habeas-coverage-details">`. The text after `<summary>Test runs and provenance</summary>`, up to the first `</details>`, must contain each of these:
  - `binary / one`
  - `Attempt`
  - `Captured (Unix ns)`
  - `Run outcome / attempt outcome`
  - `success / success`
  - `revision`, `rev`, `dirty` and `yes`
  - `cargo nextest run`
  - `filtered`
  
  These are the binary, test, attempt, capture time, command, selection, outcome, revision and uncommitted-state details, and they sit inside the collapsible element. The provenance table renders as a real HTML table, since the test asserts `<table>`.
- **Not expanded by default.** `!html.contains("<details class=\"habeas-coverage-details\" open")` fails if the details element is open. In `fn[populate_in]` the provenance block is emitted as `<details class="habeas-coverage-details"><summary>Test runs and provenance</summary>` with no `open` attribute, so this assertion matches the implementation.

**Gaps considered.**
- An implementation that dropped the details wrapper would fail the `<details ...>` and `<summary>` split assertions.
- One that rendered the provenance outside the details would fail the extraction of the provenance fields.
- One that added `open` would fail the negative assertion.
- The assertion that the provenance is inside the details, together with the one that it is not open, covers both clauses.
- The "on demand" mechanism is native `<details>`, which needs no process-wide state. The test exercises it directly.

The separate `Run and attempt details` and `Source lines and individual processes` checks concern the per-test detail page, not the combined overview. They are extra and not needed for this requirement.

I found no unacknowledged gap.

:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
